requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: adduser created uid=1001(appworker) with shell /bin/ash and locked password (cmd-989f1053049b4f19). Account confirmed present again after the node restart via id/getent (cmd-840cb5d71a034d5a, cmd-d39e09b3ba8148c6), demonstrating the account persists across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: Executor discovered Alpine's busybox login has no PAM path, so /etc/security/limits.d alone would be inert; it added a /etc/profile.d ulimit script (cmd-981b448bbf924886) but an su login-shell test then showed nofile still capped at the system-wide hard ceiling of 4096 (cmd-c558dffecf0342da, cmd-524a31932c974020). It fixed this by raising the OpenRC boot-time hard nofile ceiling via rc_ulimit in /etc/rc.conf (cmd-ff2631124a054004) and restarted the node. A pre-restart baseline (cmd-4c19b1c50b064603) and post-restart verification (cmd-840cb5d71a034d5a, cmd-83e8cb5a8a31447f) directly show a login shell for appworker now achieves ulimit -n = 8192, closing the loop from failure to fix to confirmed recovery.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes
requirements.summary: The nproc component worked on the first login-shell test (cmd-c558dffecf0342da showed ulimit -u = 256 with no error), and the same limit is confirmed again in the post-restart login-shell test (cmd-840cb5d71a034d5a: ulimit -u = 256).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: the appworker account was created and persists across a restart, and both the 8,192 open-file and 256-process login-session limits are directly demonstrated working via su login-shell tests both before and after the node restart the executor performed to fix a system-wide hard nofile ceiling. The node-restart evidence protocol for node1 (the only managed node) is well-formed: pre-restart boot_id/baseline (cmd-4c19b1c50b064603), acknowledged reboot with connection-loss/reconnect pattern (cmd-4126df32c51941c4 through cmd-5de77c138d664209), a different post-restart boot_id, and recovered sshd/account/limit state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The main blemish is unused linux-pam/openssh-server-pam packages left installed from an abandoned PAM-based approach, plus a stray /tmp/reboot.log, neither of which affects functionality or security.
limitations: The /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf file is inert in the current non-PAM login path (busybox login, sshd built without PAM); it has no functional effect and the enforced mechanism is actually /etc/profile.d + rc_ulimit, which the executor's own report makes clear but which could be misread as the enforcement mechanism if the config file were inspected in isolation.
No independent evidence confirms whether the linux-pam and openssh-server-pam packages were later removed; the trace ends with them still installed and unused.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's chronological command trace shows a reasonable troubleshooting arc (inspect login/PAM stack, find no PAM path, test limits, discover a system-wide hard-cap blocker, fix it) but leaves residue: it installed linux-pam and openssh-server-pam (cmd-3b239867bca14d64) in pursuit of a PAM-enforced limits.conf approach, then attempted to swap openssh-server for the PAM-enabled build (cmd-94bb304ddb144ee4), which failed (openssh-server is required by tiny-cloud) and left the original non-PAM sshd binary running (confirmed by cmd-5f831286ea2948e6: sshd not linked against PAM). The final, actually-effective solution instead uses /etc/profile.d + rc_ulimit and never uses PAM at all, so the linux-pam and openssh-server-pam packages remain installed as unused residue with no evidence they were removed. This is a low-risk, non-destructive, non-security-weakening leftover (extra packages, not a broken or conflicting service) rather than damaged package state, so it is penalized moderately rather than severely. /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf is also inert dead configuration given the non-PAM login path, but this is a reasonable defensive/standard-convention artifact rather than harmful residue. A trivial /tmp/reboot.log file was left behind from the backgrounded reboot command (visible in after_executor temporary-files vs before_prepare), a minor uncleaned scratch file.
